clue.text: Preservative for ocean-going sailor

parts.note: ocean-going is sea-going, so the ocean here gives sea
an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: Someone asks what keeps a seafarer's provisions from spoiling on a long voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt evaporated from seawater has long been used to cure and keep food, a classic preservative.

clue.text: Recite so strangely in secret

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the two words are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone reads a passage aloud oddly, in a private code only insiders follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is reserved for a small inner circle, hence hidden or private.

clue.text: Many left feeling aware

annotationWithheld.why: 'Many left feeling aware' (8) as held gives SENT for 'left' but nothing for the rest of SENTIENT from 'Many'; no source found to repair it

clue.text: Disembarking without personal property? Anything but!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word's synonym wraps around the second

parts.note: disembarking is landing from a ship
personal means one's own

explanation.surface: A traveller steps ashore with no possessions, and the clue protests that the truth is the very opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. The definition plays on the surface: the clue's traveller has no personal property, but the answer describes someone holding plenty of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning acres of estate is the very opposite of having no possessions at all.

clue.text: But do be more economical

explanation.surface: A plea to cut spending, opened with an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is 'except', as in all save one; the other is the command to spend less and keep money back.

clue.text: Barrier with small rope attached

parts.note: a cord is a thin rope or string
on means attached, as a lid that is on

explanation.surface: A barrier is made with a short length of rope tied to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of police or a rope line that keeps people out of an area is a barrier.

clue.text: Cautions reservists climbing into grottoes

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: grottoes are caves

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Warnings are issued to part-time soldiers scrambling up into caverns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns TA into AT before 'into' places it inside CAVES. The TA is Britain's Territorial Army, its army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a warning or proviso, so caveats are cautions.

clue.text: About to overcharge for doing no work

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
to sting someone is to overcharge them

explanation.surface: A complaint about being overcharged for a job nobody did.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idle or taking a break is at rest, not labouring.

clue.text: Herb imbibes a half-bottle while plotting it

indicators.note: imbibes means drinks in, so the herb takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb

indicators.note: half of the word bottle is its first three letters

explanation.surface: A man named Herb drinks a small bottle while scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb looks like a man's name but is the plant SAGE. The definition is loose: sabotage is the deed someone plotting would be planning.
explanation.definitionFit: Saboteurs scheme deliberate wrecking, so the deliberate wrecking is what such plotters have in mind.

clue.text: Depressing London street

explanation.surface: A bleak road in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing down is depressing; Downing Street in London is home to the British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Exhausted after late defeat

parts.note: the late means the dead, as in the late king
to beat is to defeat

explanation.surface: A player is worn out after a defeat in the closing minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead beat is an idiom for completely tired out.

clue.text: Exotic cruises do engender debate

indicators.note: exotic means foreign and unusual, signalling a strange rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Holidays on faraway cruises spark arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is formal discussion or talk, a near synonym for debate.

clue.text: Poor miner with nothing but sheep

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A penniless miner owns nothing but a few sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Merino is a breed of sheep famous for fine wool.

clue.text: Doing vast quantity of laundry? Capital!

parts.note: laundry is the washing
a ton, or tons, is a huge amount

explanation.surface: Someone faces a mountain of laundry and exclaims 'Capital!' in mock delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like an old-fashioned cheer but is the definition: a nation's capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington DC is the seat of the United States government, its capital city.

clue.text: Where a member feels at home

definitions.text: Where a member feels at home

parts.words: Where a member feels at home
parts.note: a member of Parliament is at home in the chamber of the Commons, while anyone indoors at home is under their roof

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means indoors at home, and an MP sits in the House of Commons.

clue.text: Arabian spirits are mother's ruin, they say

indicators.note: they say signals a word that is heard rather than seen

parts.note: mother's ruin is an old British nickname for gin

explanation.surface: Desert genies are blamed for a drink problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests drink, matching the gin, but the definition means supernatural beings. 'Mother's ruin' is British slang for gin, from its Victorian reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Jinn are supernatural beings of Arabian folklore, like genies.

clue.text: There are few bosses with little hair

explanation.surface: An office with a thin layer of management is compared to a balding head.
explanation.definitionFit: A company light on senior staff has sparse numbers at the head; a balding man has sparse hair on the crown.

clue.text: Sneakers are their ideal footwear

parts.note: sneakers are soft shoes, ideal for people who sneak about quietly looking for a chance to steal

explanation.definitionFit: Prowlers creep around stealthily, and soft-soled sneakers would keep them quiet.

clue.text: Soldiers' alarm

parts.note: the alarm here is a wake-up call, sounded on a bugle in camp at dawn, not a warning of danger

explanation.definitionFit: This bugle call rouses troops in the morning, the military wake-up signal.

clue.text: Duty I'm able to find in Rome

parts.note: VAT, value added tax, is a duty on goods
I'm able means I can

explanation.surface: A tourist wonders whether they can work out the sales tax while in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax. The definition is something you find in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal city state is an enclave inside the Italian capital.

clue.text: Man holding educational journal is kind of cross

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a man is male
TES is the Times Educational Supplement, a British teaching paper

explanation.surface: A man holding a teachers' paper looks irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry, but the definition is a type of cross. The TES is a British weekly for teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-pointed emblem of the Knights of Malta is one variety of cross.

clue.text: Three-noted pipe

parts.note: three musical notes: re from the sol-fa scale, then the letter names E and D
three musical notes: re from the sol-fa scale, then the letter names E and D
three musical notes: re from the sol-fa scale, then the letter names E and D

explanation.surface: A whistle that can play just three notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a simple wind instrument made from a hollow stem, a kind of pipe.

clue.text: Experimental art gave Dan dire distress

indicators.note: distress means damage, and dire makes it severe, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Modern art leaves a man called Dan deeply upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde work is innovative and pushes past convention, so it is experimental.

clue.text: Medic beset by fatigue needs to acquire tone

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the second piece wraps the first

parts.note: to fatigue is to tire
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: An exhausted doctor needs to get back in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tone' suggests muscle tone, but it is the musical sense. MB is a British medical degree, so a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the distinctive quality of a sound, its colour or tone.

clue.text: Are birds of prey what he sells?

parts.note: a hawk is a bird of prey
ER, written to stand for the sound of are, is a stretch; taken as the -er ending

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a street seller deals in falcons.
explanation.definitionFit: A street trader peddles goods door to door.

clue.text: Imply that he's a bosom pal

explanation.surface: Someone hints that a man is a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest without saying is one sense; a very close confidant is the other.

clue.text: Gather he was a merry man

explanation.surface: A call to round up the jolly outlaws.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewn fold gathers fabric; Friar Tuck was one of Robin Hood's band of Merry Men.

clue.text: Pickle everything! It's the ideal solution

parts.note: to cure meat or fish is to preserve it, like pickling
everything is all

explanation.surface: Someone declares pickling everything the answer to every problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea remedies every ill, the perfect fix.

clue.text: Academic Résumé

explanation.surface: A scholarly CV.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoretical rather than practical is one sense; a summary of a paper is the other.

clue.text: Secured by woman in the vanguard

indicators.note: in places the woman inside the other piece

parts.note: the vanguard is in the lead
she is a woman

explanation.surface: A position won by a woman at the front of the march.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog tethered on a lead is restrained, held fast.
